newsitem.title: UK: Arsonists lead N.Ireland sectarian violence.
newsitem.headline: Arsonists lead N.Ireland sectarian violence.

text.p: Arsonists struck a Roman Catholic church in rural Northern Ireland on Wednesday after a night of rioting between Catholics and Protestants in the British-ruled province.

In the latest in a string of sectarian attacks, vestments and the interior of a church at Annaclone, in County Down, were damaged by the early morning fire, the fifth in two weeks at Catholic churches, police said.

The fire followed overnight clashes between Protestants and Catholics near Lurgan, in County Armagh, where police fired plastic bullets to break up petrol bomb-throwing crowds on a road separating rival housing areas.

Northern Ireland, destablised by guerrilla conflict over the future of British rule, has experienced months of rising tension during which rival gangs have struck at Protestant and Catholic churches, community buildings, schools.

Minor damage was caused on Tuesday to a hall used by members of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity, at Stewartstown in County Tyrone. "A window was broken and a lighted rag pushed in," police said.
Last weekend eight Catholic families fled an apartment block in north Belfast after attacks by Protestant "Loyalists" who want Northern Ireland to stay British.
According to police, arsonists have damaged 53 churches, 47 community buildings and 71 schools over the past 17 months.

The province's security forces are on alert for attacks by Irish Republican Army guerrillas (IRA), fighting an escalating campaign to end rule from London and unite Northern Ireland with the neighbouring Irish Republic.
A ceasefire by Protestant guerrillas is unstable and "Loyalists" have been blamed for two killings and a spate of random attacks on Catholics in the past year.
Security sources fear more sectarian flareups in the run up to a disputed series of traditional summer marches by hardline Protestants. "It's heating up," said one officer.
Multiparty talks aimed at finding a political settlement in Northern Ireland have been suspended until a British general election, set for May 1, is over.
